reasons.hexweaver: Strengths: the boss has a named health bar with phase markers and labelled attacks, and its slams are telegraphed with clear red ground cones and circles. Loot gets light beams, rarity-coloured toasts and item stat cards, and the HUD has readable bars, cooldown numbers and a minimap. Weaknesses: the view is third-person over the shoulder, not first-person as described, and the player model is a stiff, low-detail figure. Enemies are simple blocky or primitive models, spell effects are mostly plain glowing orbs with flat sigils, and hit feedback is limited to purple and crit damage numbers, so the clip looks like a functional prototype rather than a commercial ARPG.
reasons.pyromancer: The best part is the boss fight: it has a named health bar with phase markers, named attack wind-ups (Clapper Sweep, Peal of Shards, Belfry Drop) and red ground markers, and damage numbers flag crits. The weaknesses are the visuals. Spells and the resurrection effect are made of simple shapes and flat particles, so the fire spells hardly read as fire and big moments become screen-filling yellow shapes that hide the action. Loot shows only plain green beams and small text labels, with no clear rarity colours, and only 5 of 21 drops were picked up. Enemies are simple low-poly models, and the player died twice in 60 seconds without the HUD giving a clear warning of the danger.
reasons.stormcaller: The boss fight reads well. It has a phased boss bar with named attacks ('Belfry Drop', 'Peal of Shards'), red ground circles and line telegraphs, and a clean HUD with health and mana, a cooldown spell bar, a minimap, and loot toasts colored by rarity. Outside the boss fight it falls short. Spells show up as small lightning flickers and runic circles with little weight, and most enemies are simple low-poly shapes. The damage numbers are plain, with no visible crit styling or hit-stop. About half the frames are empty traversal: the camera points at walls and there are no enemies nearby.
reasons.warden: Loot presentation works well: there are beams coloured by rarity, item labels and stat toasts, and the boss gets a bar with phases plus an enrage banner, so the clip has some ARPG structure. Weaknesses: the camera is often blocked by the player's own bubble shield and translucent beams, the market stalls look low-poly and boxy, and no ground telegraphs for enemy attacks are visible. Enemies are hard to make out in most frames, and crits and damage numbers are small and sparse, so hits don't land with much weight.
